facts.statement: The genus contains only one species, Tuebingosaurus maierfritzorum, which was originally identified as a specimen of Plateosaurus.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Tuebingosaurus maierfritzorum, originally identified as a specimen of Plateosaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, known as GPIT IV, consists of a partial postcranial skeleton.
facts.quote: The holotype, GPIT-PV-30787, also known as "GPIT IV", is a partial postcranial skeleton.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in 1922 and is stored in the paleontological collection of the University of Tübingen.
facts.quote: It was discovered in 1922 and stored in the paleontological collection of the University of Tübingen.

facts.statement: Distinctive features linking it to more derived sauropodomorphs led to its formal naming as Tuebingosaurus maierfritzorum in 2022.
facts.quote: However, it actually contains several features with more derived sauropodomorphs, which allowed it to be named as the distinct taxon Tuebingosaurus maierfritzorum in 2022.

facts.statement: In a 2025 review, researchers Sues and Schoch argued that the features distinguishing Tuebingosaurus were based on damaged bones, leading them to regard the species as a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: In their 2025 review of Triassic reptile fossils from Germany, Sues & Schoch claimed that additional review of the holotype revealed that the characters used to distinguish Tuebingosaurus from other sauropodomorphs were based on damaged bones.

facts.statement: Tuebingosaurus lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Trossingen Formation, where Tuebingosaurus fossils were found, is now understood to be a deposit of carcasses mired in a river over hundreds of years.
facts.quote: The Trossingen Formation was originally interpreted as a synchronic deposit of animals, but is now considered to be a constant accumulation of mired carcasses that were deposited over hundreds of years by a river.

rejected.statement: Tuebingosaurus, meaning "Tübingen lizard", is an extinct genus of massopodan sauropodomorph dinosaur found in the Late Triassic Trossingen Formation of Germany.
rejected.quote: Tuebingosaurus (meaning "Tübingen lizard") is an extinct genus of massopodan sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Late Triassic Trossingen Formation of Germany.
